intro: An ID index replaces repeated linear searches with direct dictionary lookups. Keeping the complete record as the value preserves every field for downstream processing.
task: Create an ID lookup and reject duplicate identifiers instead of silently overwriting.
requirements: Every record must contain id_field with a unique nonempty string value. Return a dictionary from that ID to a copied full record. Reject duplicate IDs.

Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters. Numeric values are finite Python ints or floats with magnitude at most 1e9; bool is not numeric. Plain record data may contain strings, numbers, booleans, None, lists, tuples, and dictionaries; nesting is limited to six levels and dictionaries to 1000 keys.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Check whether the ID already exists before assigning the record.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Do not silently normalize IDs; case and surrounding spaces are part of their identity.

explanation: An ID index replaces repeated linear searches with direct dictionary lookups. Keeping the complete record as the value preserves every field for downstream processing.
Duplicate identifiers make the lookup ambiguous. Detecting them during index construction prevents a later record from silently replacing an earlier one.
